subject: Game Theory
title: Salary Negotiation
description: A fast breakdown of Salary Negotiation for builders.

hook.text: Most job candidates accept the first salary offered. Those who negotiate earn 7-10% more on average.

buildup.text: Salary talks are a textbook bargaining game: the employer's budget is private, your BATNA is your backup offer.

discovery.text: Anchoring high works: candidates who name a salary first (and aim high) end up earning more.

twist.text: Women negotiate less often than men—not from weakness, but because they face social penalties for assertiveness.

climax.text: The compounding effect: a $5,000 higher starting salary adds up to $600,000 over a 40-year career.

punchline.text: Not negotiating is the most expensive choice.

quiz.question: Why is anchoring high effective in salary negotiation?
options: It sets the reference point for all discussion
